George Bell, Du'Plessis Kirifi, Anton Lienert-Brown and Jamie Hannah have been named as injury replacements Australia face their own personnel problems and will be without key centre Len Ikitau, who left Saturday's game in the first half with a head knock, while [USN:L4N45T0E6 TEXT:"Hunter Paisami"] has been suspended Jordan Petaia was also unavailable due to an ankle injury, with Corey Toole and Kadin Pritchard coming in as replacements

item.title: Guardians complete ALDS comeback, blank White Sox in Game 5
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Jose Ramirez hit a two-run homer and Gavin Williams struck out a franchise postseason-record-tying 12, leading the Cleveland Guardians to a 2-0 victory over the Chicago White Sox in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Jose Ramirez hit a two-run homer and Gavin Williams struck out a franchise postseason-record-tying 12, leading the Cleveland Guardians to a 2-0 victory over the Chicago White Sox in the decisive Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night. Cleveland became the fourth team to win a best-of-five postseason series after losing the first two games at home. Erik Sabrowski, Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith joined Williams in a combined three-hitter for the Guardians, who will meet the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series starting Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla. "This was a difficult year, and for us to be one step away from the World Series, our ultimate goal, this is really exciting," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. Chicago struck out 21 times, the most in major league history for a nine-inning postseason game. That broke the record of 19 the White Sox set in their Game 3 loss on Wednesday. "We're all bummed and sad, knowing we probably should have got the job done," White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery said after the loss. Ramirez sent starter Sean Burke's knuckle curve 348 feet over the right-field wall, scoring Steven Kwan, who led off the fourth with the game's first hit. The 78 mph pitch was well below the strike zone, but Ramirez golfed it inside the foul pole, giving him seven RBIs over the final three games of the series. "Jose is Jose, we all love him. He always has that one moment all the time," Williams said. "We know what he's going to do." "Obviously, it came down to one pitch to Ramirez," Burke added. "He's a really good player. He's probably going to be in the Hall of Fame some day. But it's frustrating." Williams (1-0) carried a no-hitter into the sixth -- two days after recording the final three outs in Game 4 -- before Kyle Teel laced a two-out single. Williams, who had hit Colson Montgomery to open the sixth, walked Miguel Vargas after Teel's hit. Sabrowski entered and struck out Munetaka Murakami to end the inning. Williams worked 5 2/3 innings, allowing one hit and walking two. The right-hander's 24 strikeouts over three appearances were one shy of the Division Series record set by Gerrit Cole of the Houston Astros in 2019. Williams matched the Cleveland single-game postseason record of 12 strikeouts, set by Charles Nagy in the 1996 ALDS against the Baltimore Orioles. Williams owns two of the five double-digit strikeout performances in team playoff history. "It's pretty satisfying," Williams said. "No matter what point (of the postseason) it is, it's always fun. And just being able to celebrate with the guys, it's a dream come true." Burke (1-1) allowed two runs on four hits over five innings, striking out four. Smith, who pitched the final 1 2/3 innings for his first save of the postseason, and Gaddis appeared in all five games. "Our back end of the bullpen has been the lifeblood of this team since I've been here," Vogt said. "They have the highest leverage. They have the toughest outs to get. And Eric came in, you just felt like he was going to do what he did." --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: River Plate vence a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que sella su descenso en liga argentina
item.description: River Plate volvió al triunfo el sábado al vencer 1-0 como local a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que selló su descenso a la segunda división del fútbol argentino.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: River Plate volvió al triunfo el sábado al vencer 1-0 como local a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, que selló su descenso a la segunda división del fútbol argentino. Con la victoria en la duodécima jornada del Torneo Clausura, River llegó a 16 puntos y se ubicó novenol en la tabla de posiciones de la Zona B, a dos unidades de los ocho puestos de clasificación a la postemporada. En el partido disputado en el estadio Monumental ante 85.000 aficionados, el gol lo anotó el defensor Marcos Acuña a los seis minutos de juego, tras un centro de Ángel Correa. "Fue una victoria importante. El equipo jugó un buen partido y logramos el triunfo, aunque no pudimos ampliar la diferencia y cerrar el partido", dijo el delantero Lautaro Pereyra a la televisión local. Por su parte, a falta de cuatro fechas para el final de la fase regular, Estudiantes se convirtió en el primer equipo en confirmar el descenso tras una campaña con dos victorias, cinco empates y 21 derrotas. "Peleamos todo el año, pero nunca pudimos hacer pie. Errores, mala suerte, y termina pasando lo que no queríamos un par de fechas antes", dijo el defensor de Estudiantes Gonzalo Maffini tras la derrota. En otros partidos del sábado, Barracas Central superó 2-0 como local a Huracán y Banfield ganó 2-1 en su visita a Tigre, mientras que Central Córdoba y Estudiantes de La Plata igualaron 2-2. El viernes, Boca Juniors igualó 2-2 ante Instituto de Córdoba, Defensa y Justicia venció 2-0 a Unión y Sarmiento superó 3-1 a Aldosivi, en tanto que Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata y Atlético Tucumán empataron 1-1.

item.title: L'armée américaine met hors d'usage un navire dans le golfe d'Oman
item.description: L'armée américaine a déclaré samedi avoir mis hors d'usage un navire commercial dans le Golfe d'Oman après que l'équipage, ignorant des avertissements, a tenté de forcer le blocus naval imposé par les Etats-Unis contre l'Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'armée américaine a déclaré samedi avoir mis hors d'usage un navire commercial dans le Golfe d'Oman après que l'équipage, ignorant des avertissements, a tenté de forcer le blocus naval imposé par les Etats-Unis contre l'Iran. "Un avion de chasse de l'armée américaine a frappé la poupe du M/V Ocean Molica (également connu sous le nom d''Arika Sun'), battant pavillon panaméen, à l'aide d'une munition à guidage de précision, rendant ainsi le système de propulsion du navire totalement hors d'usage, sans blesser l'équipage", a indiqué le commandement central de l'armée américaine (Centcom) sur le réseau social X. Le Centcom a indiqué que le navire avait tenté de traverser les eaux régionales après avoir quitté un port iranien.

item.title: Canadiens blank Red Wings in rare 1-0 shootout victory
item.description: Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give the host Montreal Canadiens a 1-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give the host Montreal Canadiens a 1-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night. Jacob Fowler made 30 saves in regulation and overtime for the Canadiens, who snapped their three-game losing streak (0-2-1). Daniil Tarasov also stopped 30 shots in the first 65 minutes for the Red Wings, who dropped their second in two nights (0-1-1). It was the second career shutout for both goaltenders. The Canadiens had three goals called back. Alexandre Texier's apparent overtime winner 2:37 into the extra period was overturned by an offside challenge from Detroit coach Todd McLellan. Bolduc was offside. An apparent goal by Cole Caufield 1:16 into the game was reversed by video review because the puck did not completely cross the goal line. Bolduc put the puck into the net 7:05 into the second period, but the goal was immediately waved off because of goalie interference by Jake Evans. There were chants from the Montreal crowd of "We want Larkin" at times when the Red Wings' Dylan Larkin was on the ice, but booed him during his shootout attempt, which was stopped by Fowler. It was first reported on June 4, that Larkin asked to be traded and was removed as the team's captain at the beginning of training camp. Bolduc hit the goal post with 8:07 left in the first period. Fowler made a big save on Alex DeBrincat's wide-open backhand attempt from just below the left circle with a little less than five minutes remaining in the second period and stopped Andrew Copp on a breakaway attempt 3:37 into the third. Tarasov denied a shot that deflected off of Caufield just outside the crease at the 6:09 mark of the third period. Montreal defenseman Kaiden Guhle made his season debut after undergoing adductor muscle surgery over the summer. --Field Level

item.title: Brandon Hagel (hat trick), Lightning down Islanders for 4th straight win
item.description: Tampa Bay's Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as the Lightning claimed their fourth straight victory, beating the host New York Islanders 5-3 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tampa Bay's Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as the Lightning claimed their fourth straight victory, beating the host New York Islanders 5-3 on Saturday night. Tied 3-all, Hagel rifled a shot past Ilya Sorokin (21 saves) with a long wrister for his second goal and added his third into an empty net as Tampa Bay won the first of its two-game set in New York. He added an assist for a four-point night. Jake Guentzel tallied twice, and Nikita Kucherov and Max Crozier each had two assists. Goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots. Defenseman Tony DeAngelo recorded a goal and an assist, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Brayden Schenn scored as the Islanders lost for the first time in three games on home ice this season. New York forward Matias Maccelli had his 121st career assist in his 300th NHL game. A turnover led to the first goal as Pageau flipped a puck from the end boards out near the right circle in his defensive end. Guentzel gained possession and sent in an unassisted tally at 5:45 of the first period. Vasilevskiy kept the Islanders off the scoreboard by denying Bo Horvat on a breakaway after Tampa Bay defenseman Victor Hedman gave away the puck. Horvat fired a shot on the 1-on-1 try, but the Vezina Trophy winner turned it away at 11:14. A 36-goal scorer last season, Hagel watched Hedman backhand a long flip down the ice and used his speed to run it down. He beat defenseman Ryan Pulock to the puck and tallied at 15:42 for a two-goal lead through the opening period. Despite being banged up, New York's blue line put the club on the board in the second period when DeAngelo took a feed from Ondrej Palat and fired home his first goal from the deep slot at 6:27. Guentzel netted his second with his team on the power play. Kucherov found him to the left of Sorokin, and the winger made an inside move and beat the goalie for his third marker at 7:54 for a 3-1 advantage. Pageau made up for his earlier miscue to cut the Islanders' deficit to 3-2 at 11:41 of the second period. On Schaefer's deep shot, Pageau tipped it past Vasilevskiy. In the final moments of the second, Horvat helped tie it when his pass through the crease went in around a tangle of players near Vasilevskiy while the Islanders were on a power play. Schenn was credited with his second score of the season. Hagel broke the tie with 1:44 remaining in regulation, then completed his hat trick with an empty-net goal 21 seconds later to seal the victory. --Field Level Media

item.title: Senators rally from early 2-goal deficit, beat Predators in shootout
item.description: Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as the Ottawa Senators rallied for a 3-2 win over the visiting Nashville Predators on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as the Ottawa Senators rallied for a 3-2 win over the visiting Nashville Predators on Saturday. Tim Stutzle had a goal and an assist in regulation and scored in the second round of the shootout. Drake Batherson also scored for the Senators, while Ottawa goaltender Linus Ullmark stopped 16 shots. Ross Colton and Jonathan Marchessault scored first-period goals, and Ryan O'Reilly had a shootout goal for Nashville. Murray recorded 18 saves in his first start since the 2023-24 season, when he played for the Dallas Stars. Ullmark saved Steven Stamkos' final shootout attempt to secure the win. Earlier in the third, with an extra attacker on the ice, Stutzle's shot deflected off Pinto and ricocheted off Batherson's shin to tie the game at 2-2 at 18:37. The Predators struck first at 8:50 of the opening period when a loose puck emerged from a crowd near the left circle. Colton collected it and snapped a quick shot past Ullmark into the top-right corner of the net. Marchessault doubled Nashville's lead on the power play at 13:10. Taking a pass from Stamkos just below the left circle, Marchessault turned and fired, slipping a shot between Ullmark's stick and the post to make it 2-0. Ottawa cut its deficit to 2-1 on a power-play goal at 9:29 of the second period. Dylan Cozens slid a cross-ice pass to Stutzle, who rifled a one-timer into the net. Murray gloved Cozens' shot at 13:40 of the second period. Moments later, Thomas Chabot's wrist shot through traffic rang off the left post. Later in the second period, the Predators killed off Ottawa's 5-on-3 advantage. The Predators killed off a power play to open overtime, and as Roman Josi emerged from the penalty box, he collected a rebound at center ice and skated in alone on Ullmark, who turned aside his shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rickard Rakell lifts Penguins over Stars with shootout winner
item.description: Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and the Penguins beat the Dallas Stars 2-1 Saturday night in Pittsburgh.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and the Penguins beat the Dallas Stars 2-1 Saturday night in Pittsburgh. Dallas forced overtime when Tyler Seguin tied it 1-1 with 30 seconds left in regulation after Roope Hintz won a faceoff and Seguin deflected Jason Robertson's shot past Arturs Silovs. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby also tallied in the shootout for the Penguins while Seguin and Wyatt Johnston scored for Dallas. After Rakell's goal put Pittsburgh up, Silovs deflected Mikko Rantanen's shot to end it. Connor Dewar scored his first goal of the season for the Penguins, who were playing the second of a back-to-back and had lost three straight (0-2-1). Silovs made 24 saves. Jake Oettinger made 19 saves for Dallas, which had won two straight. Oettinger, who came in with consecutive shutouts, saw his shutout streak end at 188:52, the third longest in franchise history. Crosby is still looking for his first regulation goal six games into the season. Pittsburgh was 0-for-5 on the power play; Dallas was 0-for-3. The Penguins appeared to take a 1-0 lead late in the first period when Stars forward Justin Hryckowian tapped a loose puck into his own net during a scramble in front. But it was ruled that Pittsburgh's Hendrix Lapierre used a high stick earlier in the sequence. Silovs robbed Seguin with his left pad with 4:25 remaining in the second period to keep the game scoreless. Oettinger made a superb glove save against Crosby in the slot in the opening minute of the third period. Dewar made It 1-0 at 1:57 of the third period. He carried the puck into the zone along the left boards, cut across the slot and lifted a backhand that deflected off Dallas defenseman Lian Bichsel's stick and over Oettinger's right shoulder. Oettinger made a pair of saves on Evgeni Malkin in the final minute of overtime. --Field Level Media

item.title: Canadian ransomware negotiator arrested amid FBI hacker crackdown
item.description: A Canadian ransomware negotiator was arrested Thursday and faces unspecified extortion charges, according to court documents, prison records and a person familiar with the matter, as the FBI cracks down on a hacking group that stole information about its employees.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: A Canadian ransomware negotiator was arrested Thursday and faces unspecified extortion charges, according to court documents, prison records and a person familiar with the matter, as the FBI cracks down on a hacking group that stole information about its employees. Edward Dubrovsky faces charges of conspiracy to "threaten to impair the confidentiality of information with intent to extort money" and "interference with commerce," according to court documents filed with the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, which covers Philadelphia. The records, which are partially sealed, provide conflicting spellings of his last name — "Dobrovsky" or "Dobrosky" — and do not identify his age, profession, or employer. A person briefed on the matter said the person was Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky. Federal prosecutors in Philadelphia did not return repeated messages seeking comment about the discrepancies. Attempts to reach Dubrovsky and his attorneys were unsuccessful. Repeated attempts to reach the company displayed on Dubrovsky's LinkedIn profile, CyberSteward, were similarly unsuccessful. CyberSteward advertises itself online as specializing in "threat actor engagement, cyber-extortions, complex negotiations, and settlement facilitation." On LinkedIn, Dubrovsky presents himself as a specialist in the process of negotiating with cybercriminals over ransom payments. Electronic wallet records leaked in 2010 and preserved by dark-web intelligence firm District 4 Labs identify Dubrovsky as a resident of Richmond Hill, north of Toronto, and put his current age at 54. Federal prison records show that a 54-year-old named Edward Dubrovsky is currently being detained at a federal detention center in Philadelphia. News of Dubrovsky's arrest was earlier reported by Politico and independent journalist Brian Krebs . The arrest comes as the Federal Bureau of Investigation is leading a global crackdown on the hacking group ShinyHunters, which rattled the bureau last month by stealing information on what it said was [USN:L6N45E0VU TEXT:"nearly every FBI employee"]. When Reuters asked the FBI about Dubrovsky's arrest, it referred the news agency to FBI Director Kash Patel's [USN:L6N45V0R8 TEXT:"statement on Friday"] revealing that the bureau had arrested a "suspected co-conspirator of the ShinyHunters group" and declined further comment.

item.title: William Nylander (5 points) propels Maple Leafs past Avalanche
item.description: William Nylander had two goals and three assists, Auston Matthews had two goals and two assists, and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3 in Denver on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: William Nylander had two goals and three assists, Auston Matthews had two goals and two assists, and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3 in Denver on Saturday night. Nylander's three assists and five points matched his career highs. Easton Cowan and Nick Blankenburg also scored, Nick Paul had two assists and Sergei Bobrovsky turned away 30 shots for Toronto. The Maple Leafs have split the first two games of their three-game road trip. Nathan MacKinnon had two goals, Brock Nelson also scored and Mackenzie Blackwood had 17 saves for Colorado. The Avalanche lost for the first time in three home games this season. Blankenburg gave Toronto the early advantage when he scored from close range at 3:03 of the first period, but MacKinnon asserted himself the rest of the period. He took a pass from Brett Kulak in the neutral zone, skated through the Maple Leafs defense and slid the puck through Bobrovsky's pads at 10:46 to tie it. MacKinnon gave Colorado a 2-1 lead later in the period when his screened shot from between the faceoff circles beat Bobrovsky high to the stick side at 15:14. The Avalanche had a chance to extend the lead with consecutive power plays at the start of the second but couldn't score. Toronto took advantage of its first power-play chance when Nylander got a pass from Gavin McKenna to the right of Blackwood, deked the goaltender and tucked the puck on the opposite side at 6:53. Colorado took a 3-2 lead later in the second when Nelson cleaned up his own rebound and fluttered a shot over Bobrovsky at 12:25, but the Maple Leafs responded twice in less than a minute. Nylander's second of the night, at 16:47, tied the game, and Cowan made it 4-3 with a one-timer on a pass from Morgan Rielly at 17:33. Matthews scored a power-play goal at 12:02 of the third period and added an empty-netter in the final minute after Blackwood came off for an extra skater. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blues snap 3-game skid, score season-high 5 goals to edge Blue Jackets
item.description: Jimmy Snuggerud scored two second-period goals in quick succession and Jonatan Berggren scored the game-winning goal to help the St. Louis Blues halt their three-game slide with a 5-3 home victory over the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jimmy Snuggerud scored two second-period goals in quick succession and Jonatan Berggren scored the game-winning goal to help the St. Louis Blues halt their three-game slide with a 5-3 home victory over the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday. The Blues entered the matchup buried in offensive woes during their three-game losing skid, but found their flow as Jake Neighbours and Pavel Buchnevich also found the back of the net and Dylan Holloway picked up three assists. Jordan Binnington made 20 saves as he recorded his first victory of the season. Cole Sillinger, Kent Johnson, and Valeri Nichushkin lit the lamp for the Blue Jackets, while Jet Greaves finished with 22 saves. With a delayed penalty forthcoming, Berggren went hard to the front of the net and found a loose puck to score the eventual game-winning goal with just over 10 minutes remaining. After a quiet start to the contest, the Blue Jackets broke the deadlock with 3:50 left in the first period as Erik Gudbranson sent a pass that redirected off the side of the net and Sean Monahan's shot banked in off Nichushkin for his first goal as a Blue Jacket. Johnson doubled up the lead with 12 seconds left in the opening frame as he cut into the middle and wired a shot off the far post and past Binnington. Neighbours made it a one-goal game with 13:50 remaining in the middle frame as he found the puck near the Blue Jackets' net and fired it home. Snuggerud knotted things up just under three minutes later as Philip Broberg carried the puck in wide and slid a pass across that hit the young forward's skate and bounced in. The 2022 first-round pick kept it rolling with his second of the night with 7:28 left in the second as he patiently waited and then perfectly placed a shot under the blocker of Greaves. Sillinger took advantage of some poor rebound control from Binnington to tie the game back up with 13:09 left in the third period. Buchnevich put the game to rest with an empty-net goal. Each team only had one power-play chance on the night and neither was successful. --Field Level Media

item.title: Big second period propels Hurricanes past Blackhawks
item.description: Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook both scored once and added an assist, and the visiting Carolina Hurricanes used a three-goal second period to beat the slumping Chicago Blackhawks 5-2 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook both scored once and added an assist, and the visiting Carolina Hurricanes used a three-goal second period to beat the slumping Chicago Blackhawks 5-2 on Saturday night. Mark Jankowski, Sebastian Aho and Taylor Hall also scored for the Hurricanes, who have won four straight games. All four Carolina forward lines lit the lamp. Goaltender Brandon Bussi made 24 saves and Mike Reilly collected two assists. Roman Kantserov, with his first NHL goal, and Oliver Moore replied for the Blackhawks, while goalie Spencer Knight made 34 saves. Chicago has just one win in six games to start the season. After dominating play from the drop of the puck, the Hurricanes finally pulled ahead when Jankowski converted a breakaway with 56.2 seconds remaining in the first period. He has scored in three consecutive games for the first time in his 11-year NHL career. That tally sparked the defending Stanley Cup champions. Aho doubled the lead when he buried a shot from the slot after neatly eluding a check at 2:09 of the second period. Blake gave the visitors a three-goal lead 79 seconds later by converting from the doorstep for his first goal of the season. Kantserov provided the Blackhawks a boost when he tallied on a breakaway for his milestone marker, a huge boost for the 2023 second-round draft pick, at 4:40 of the middle frame. However, Hall restored Carolina's three-goal lead 85 seconds later by unloading a one-timer from the high slot. Martinook extended the edge with his first of the season, a backhanded shot from the slot at 5:00 of the third period. Moore rounded out the scoring with less than six minutes remaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kipchoge wins first marathon in three years in Melbourne
item.description: Kenya's twice Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge won the Melbourne Marathon in a course record of 2 hours, 9 minutes and 10 seconds on Sunday, claiming his 17th win over the distance at age 41.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya's twice Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge won the Melbourne Marathon in a course record of 2 hours, 9 minutes and 10 seconds on Sunday, claiming his 17th win over the distance at age 41. Kipchoge is attempting to run a marathon on all seven continents over two years, having launched his continental campaign at the Cape Town Marathon [USN:L1N3ZX0XB TEXT:"in May"]. Sunday's win was his first in three years, after he won Berlin in 2023 for [USN:L2N3VP0S3 TEXT:"a record"] 11th title at the majors. "I believe that my body is still peaking – still able to compete with the next generation," Kipchoge told reporters after the race. "The oldest athlete is still competing but I am happy to run with the Gen Zs. I (increased) the pace after 30 km, to see whether I can run well and beat the (race record). My plan went well." Australian Thomas Do Canto finished second behind Kipchoge at 2:10:35, while compatriot Reece Edwards was third at 2:14:33. New Zealand's Camille French won the women's race in 2:28:25, followed by Australian Sinead Diver at 2:28:49 and Nichola Sheridan of Ireland at 2:29:13.

item.title: US military says it disabled cargo vessel trying to run Iran blockade
item.description: The US military said on Saturday it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after the ship's crew ignored warnings and attempted to run a naval blockade against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US military said on Saturday it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after the ship's crew ignored warnings and attempted to run a naval blockade against Iran. "A U.S. military fighter jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also known as the “Arika Sun”) with a precision munition, fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew," the US Central Command posted on X. CENTCOM said the cargo vessel had attempted to transit regional waters after leaving an Iranian port. Reuters was not immediately able to reach the bulk carrier's operator for comment. CENTCOM warned mariners in the Gulf of Oman and the approaches to the Strait of Hormuz to heed blockade warnings, monitor notice-to-mariners broadcasts and contact US naval forces. The number of vessels [USN:L1N45U0AH TEXT:"transiting"] the vital strait fell to the lowest in more than two months after attacks on tankers reached their highest level last week since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, raising concerns over shipping disruptions and supporting crude prices. Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz carried 20% of the world's oil consumption.

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore questionable, DT Ed Oliver out vs. Rams
item.description: Buffalo Bills receiver DJ Moore was a limited practice participant on Saturday due to his shoulder injury and was listed as questionable for Monday night's road game against the Los Angeles Rams.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Buffalo Bills receiver DJ Moore was a limited practice participant on Saturday due to his shoulder injury and was listed as questionable for Monday night's road game against the Los Angeles Rams. Star defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee) and receiver Joshua Palmer (shoulder) were ruled out by the Bills. Palmer was added to the report on Friday and missed Saturday's session. Moore injured his left shoulder for the second time this season in the second quarter of last Sunday's 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots. Oliver was injured in the third quarter against New England. Moore, 29, has 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown in four games this season. He was obtained in the offseason from the Chicago Bears. Oliver, 28, has nine tackles, one fumble recovery and half a sack in three games this season. Cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) and defensive lineman Landon Jackson (knee) are also questionable for Buffalo. For the Rams, safety Quentin Lake (hip) is questionable. Star defensive lineman Aaron Donald (back) didn't practice Saturday but is good to go for the contest. Also, Los Angeles coach Sean McVay said defensive end Myles Garrett is progressing from knee surgery but the team is unlikely to open his 21-day practice window next week. Garrett struggled in the season-opening loss against the San Francisco 49ers and cited knee irritation as a factor. The Rams placed him on injured reserve on Sept. 17. "He's making good progress," McVay told reporters. "As far as what that timeline looks like, it's kind of week-to-week in terms of how he feels. But I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week." Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year, was acquired from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kirill Kaprizov nets hat trick as Wild hand Panthers rare loss
item.description: Kirill Kaprizov tallied his seventh career hat trick and added an assist, and the Minnesota Wild pulled away for a 4-1 win over the Florida Panthers on Saturday evening in Sunrise, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kirill Kaprizov tallied his seventh career hat trick and added an assist, and the Minnesota Wild pulled away for a 4-1 win over the Florida Panthers on Saturday evening in Sunrise, Fla. Matt Boldy finished with a goal and an assist for Minnesota, which snapped a two-game winless skid. Quinn Hughes was one of four other Wild players to tally an assist. Matthew Tkachuk scored the lone goal for Florida. The outcome marked the Panthers' first loss in regulation in five games this season. Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 of 30 shots to earn the victory. Panthers goaltender Jacob Markstrom allowed three goals on 28 shots. Minnesota jumped out to a 1-0 lead in the first minute of the game. Boldy carried the puck into the offensive zone and fired a wrist shot above Markstrom's left shoulder 53 seconds in. The Wild increased their lead to 2-0 with a power-play goal at 6:18 of the first period. Maxim Shabanov fed a cross-ice pass to Kaprizov, who buried a one-timer from the right circle. Florida cut the deficit to 2-1 at 2:18 of the second period. Tkachuk kept the puck on a two-on-one rush but his shot was kicked out by Wallstedt. Tkachuk followed the rebound and scored on his second chance from near the front of the crease. Kaprizov struck again to boost the Wild's lead to 3-1 at 5:00 of the second. He scored on a wrist shot from the right circle. The Wild's top scorer finished his hat trick with an empty-net goal at 18:56 of the third. Kaprizov got the puck in Minnesota's defensive zone and flipped a long shot into the open net for his sixth goal in five games this season. Wild forward Rieger Lorenz made his NHL debut. The 22-year-old Calgary native was Minnesota's second-round pick (No. 56 overall) in the 2022 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: South Korea completes Arctic-Europe commercial voyage, eyes regular service despite risks
item.description: A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday, as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub.
item.dc:creator: Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday, as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub. The PanStar Acro docked in the southeastern port 50 days after setting sail on August 22. Authorities say the Arctic route could cut typical voyage times by around a third. President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030. But the project [USN:L1N44J01G TEXT:"risks friction"] with Western allies hoping to keep Russia isolated during its war in Ukraine. The route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, and Seoul consulted with Moscow about the journey, including whether the ship needed help to tackle any problems, such as getting stuck in ice. On its outbound voyage, the vessel passed through Arctic waters and reached its first European port, Felixstowe in Britain, before calling at Rotterdam and Gdansk and returning home via the Arctic. The trial voyage also highlighted the challenges ahead. Before the departure, PanStar told Reuters it was seeking about 1,300 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo, but the ship left with 737 TEU of cargo plus empty containers. Industry experts have said the route's value will depend on reliable schedules, the costs of slowing to avoid ice, special insurance premiums and extra fuel use.

item.title: Real's Vinicius apologises after red card for hair pull against Villarreal
item.description: Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr has apologised to his teammates and the club's fans after being sent off in the 1-0 win over Villarreal in LaLiga at the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr has apologised to his teammates and the club's fans after being sent off in the [USN:L6N45W060 TEXT:"1-0 win over Villarreal"] in LaLiga at the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday. Vinicius now faces a nervous wait for the ruling of the disciplinary committee, which could see him miss Real's fixture with rivals Barcelona on October 25 at Camp Nou. The Brazilian thought he had scored Real's second goal but his effort was disallowed after a VAR review found he should be dismissed for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up. After the match, Vinicius, who came on in the 52nd minute and was red carded 20 minutes later, posted on social media, saying, "sorry to the team and the fans." Spanish Football Federation regulations state that pulling an opponent's hair is regarded as violent conduct. The sanction for violent conduct without causing injury to an opponent (Article 130) is a ban of one to three matches. Real's next three LaLiga games are against Sevilla, Barca and Racing Santander, but missing El Clasico would be a bitter blow for the 26-year-old Brazil international.

item.title: Justice Department probes TV networks over Trump pool boycott
item.description: The US Justice Department said on Saturday it is investigating whether television networks violated federal antitrust laws over their decision to boycott covering the White House following its decision to pull the credentials of reporters from three news organizations, including CNN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department said on Saturday it is investigating whether television networks violated federal antitrust laws over their decision to boycott covering the White House following its decision to pull the credentials of reporters from three news organizations, including CNN. The networks under investigation are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News, the Justice Department said. "Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act," a Justice Department spokesperson said. "The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws." The investigation is the latest in a series of clashes between the Trump administration and major news organizations. President Donald Trump has repeatedly called the mainstream media "fake news" and frequently clashes with reporters during encounters with the press. The action also puts legal and potentially financial pressure on the media to continue coverage of the president even when they disagree with how the White House handles them. The networks did not immediately respond to requests from Reuters for comment. The New York Times was first to report about the probe. The investigation comes after weeks of tension between the White House and the press. CREDENTIALS REVOKED IN SEPTEMBER On September 19, the White House blocked reporters from CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from entering the building, revoking their credentials. The White House said covering the president was a "privilege – not a right.” The outlets sued the administration, alleging the exclusions violated the First Amendment and that the White House was retaliating over their coverage. CNN is one of the five news organizations — along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC — that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organizing coverage and share the footage with outlets around the country. All of the five television networks that cover the White House, including Fox News, suspended coverage in solidarity and refused to provide replacement coverage. The White House reinstated the credentials on September 24 after US District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the ban was likely unconstitutional and ordered the administration to "immediately return, reinstate, and restore" their access. However, disputes over access to specific presidential events and pool assignments continued afterward.

item.title: Macklin Celebrini scores in return, but Oilers stifle Sharks
item.description: Tristan Jarry made 19 saves as the Edmonton Oilers skated to a 3-1 win against the host San Jose Sharks on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tristan Jarry made 19 saves as the Edmonton Oilers skated to a 3-1 win against the host San Jose Sharks on Saturday afternoon. Mattias Ekholm, Vasily Podkolzin and Alex Formenton scored while Connor McDavid increased his early-season points total to 13 with an assist for the Oilers, who have won four straight games since dropping their season opener to the Vancouver Canucks. Macklin Celebrini's first goal of the season was the lone score for the Sharks, who have dropped two of their last three. Celebrini, who missed two games with a lower-body injury, led San Jose with 21:59 of ice time and placed two shots on goal. Yaroslav Askarov made 17 saves. Ekholm put Edmonton up 1-0 at 12:37 of the first period. Isaac Howard set Ekholm up for a slap shot through traffic from between the faceoff circles. San Jose and Edmonton each had five shots on goal in the first frame, while the Sharks out-hit the Oilers 17-7. The Oilers didn't register a shot on goal in the second period until 6:09 remained. Celebrini almost tied the game 1-1 with five seconds left in the frame, but his shot rang off the post. Podkolzin increased Edmonton's lead to 2-0 at 3:13 of the third period. After an Oilers power play expired, McDavid set Podkolzin up with a backward pass and the winger scored on a slap shot. Formenton added to Edmonton's tally with a backhanded shot past Askarov to make the score 3-0 at 5:40. Celebrini put the Sharks on the board 3-1 at 11:19. Michael Misa set up the goal with a backhanded pass from against the boards and Celebrini scored on a wrist shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: US will learn from bruising friendly defeat by Spain, says Hayes
item.description: US women's coach Emma Hayes shook off a dismal 2-0 defeat on Saturday in the first of two friendlies against Spain, with the Americans building towards next month's World Cup qualifiers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US women's coach Emma Hayes shook off a dismal 2-0 defeat on Saturday in the first of two friendlies against Spain, with the Americans building towards next month's World Cup qualifiers. The match between top-ranked Spain and the Olympic champions was billed as a marquee showdown but the visitors took control as Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored inside 15 minutes. Spain's Adriana Nanclares saved a second-half penalty from Lily Yohannes to keep a clean sheet for the world champions. "When you play the best team in the world you have to execute everything really well in the first instance," said Hayes. "Did I think we did enough to score a goal? Of course we did. Did we do enough to score more than one? Absolutely. "We just didn't make necessarily the right decision and execute with the quality I know we should have." The US had 10 shots on target to three from Spain, who had Athenea Del Castillo sent off in added time for pulling Michelle Cooper's hair three minutes after coming off the bench. Hayes said that efficiency would be a key target for the US when the two sides play again on Tuesday. "We create the most chances in world football. But finishing, we do not do that in world football," Hayes told reporters. "So I wasn't concerned about us creating today, and I'm not concerned about us finishing. You just have to lock in, get the details right, and keep working on it." The US aim to qualify for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil via the Concacaf W Championship, three years after their worst performance at the global tournament where they exited in the last 16 and Spain staked their territory as the world's finest. Briton Hayes' arrival [USN:L8N3C60IU TEXT:"months later"] from Chelsea sparked a renaissance for the US, who collected gold in Paris and welcomed back veteran [USN:L6N45L15G TEXT:"Mallory Swanson"] to camp this month. "We've got some really, really good players and we're a really good team regardless of the result today," said Hayes. "I think we're much closer to them than we were three years ago."

item.title: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava (leg) leaves game vs. Oregon
item.description: UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava suffered an apparent leg injury just before halftime of the No. 21 Bruins' Big Ten Conference game at No. 13 Oregon on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava suffered an apparent leg injury just before halftime of the No. 21 Bruins' Big Ten Conference game at No. 13 Oregon on Saturday. Iamaleava did not come out with the UCLA offense on its first drive after intermission. Backup Ty Dieffenbach took over. Iamaleava returned to the sideline in street clothes during the third quarter, signaling the end of his day. Iamaleava committed three turnovers in the first half, including an interception thrown into the end zone on his final play. It was the second pick Iamaleava threw in less than two minutes. He appeared to have suffered the injury on the first one. He got up gingerly with the help of UCLA training staff after taking a hit from Oregon defensive lineman Bear Alexander. Jerry Mixon intercepted Iamaleava's under-duress throw. Iamaleava finished 10-for-17 passing for 162 yards, no touchdowns and the two interceptions. He also lost a fumble inside the Bruins' 10, which led to an Oregon touchdown, in the first quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Patriots place WR Mack Hollins (calf) on injured reserve
item.description: The New England Patriots placed leading receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve Saturday due to a calf injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New England Patriots placed leading receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve Saturday due to a calf injury. Hollins is required to miss at least four games. He leads New England in receptions (15) and receiving yardage (209). Hollins, 33, was injured during the third quarter of last week's 29-26 victory over the Buffalo Bills. The injury to Hollins comes with A.J. Brown (ankle) already on the injured list. New England's receivers group against the visiting Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday will consist of Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. The Patriots also placed fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle/knee) on IR. New England also activated special teams standout Brenden Schooler (back) from the non-football injured list, signed cornerback Kindle Vildor to the 53-man roster and elevated linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Elliott Davison from the practice squad for Sunday's game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Oklahoma stuns No. 1 Texas on walk-off field goal
item.description: Tate Sandell hit a 47-yard field goal with no time left on the clock to give Oklahoma a 27-24 upset of No. 1 Texas on Saturday in Dallas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tate Sandell hit a 47-yard field goal with no time left on the clock to give Oklahoma a 27-24 upset of No. 1 Texas on Saturday in Dallas. Courtland Guillory intercepted Arch Manning at the Oklahoma 39 with 19 seconds left in regulation to give the Sooners (3-2, 1-1 Southeastern Conference) a shot. Completions of 13 and 20 yards from John Mateer to Isaiah Sategna gave Sandell the chance to win it. The win was Oklahoma's first over the Longhorns (4-1, 1-1 SEC) since 2023 and its first over a top-ranked opponent since beating Missouri in the 2007 Big 12 Championship Game. Oklahoma had never before beaten a No. 1 opponent when unranked. Manning finished 19 of 31 for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but he also threw two interceptions that helped sink the Longhorns, who outgained the Sooners 382-238. No. 2 Georgia 20, No. 6 Alabama 17 Gunner Stockton threw for 249 yards and a touchdown while rushing for another score to help the Bulldogs earn a victory over the Crimson Tide in Tuscaloosa, Ala. Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for a career-high 120 yards for Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC), which posted its first regular-season win over Alabama since 2007 -- also the last victory for the Bulldogs in Tuscaloosa. Peyton Woodring's 23-yard field goal with 5:25 left proved to be the game-winning play. Keelon Russell completed 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and a touchdown for Alabama (5-1, 3-1), which was outgained 455-346 and trailed 10-0 before jumping ahead 14-10 at halftime on EJ Crowell's 1-yard TD run on the final play of the first half. No. 3 Notre Dame 58, Stanford 7 Jonaz Walton rushed for 181 yards and two touchdowns, including a 97-yard scoring run, and the host Fighting Irish pummeled the Cardinal in South Bend, Ind. CJ Carr completed 14 of 20 passes for 181 yards and three touchdowns for Notre Dame (6-0), which never trailed. Nolan James Jr. rushed for 73 yards and two scores. Davis Warren completed 12 of 22 passes for 144 yards with one touchdown and one interception for Stanford (2-4), which was outgained 598-202, including 361-58 on the ground. No. 5 Ohio State 45, Maryland 16 Julian Sayin threw four first-half touchdown passes, two to Jeremiah Smith, and the Buckeyes rolled past the Terrapins in Columbus, Ohio. Sayin passed for 203 yards in the first 30 minutes as the Buckeyes (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) took a 31-10 halftime lead. Smith's first TD, the 37th of his career, tied Michigan's Anthony Carter for second all-time in the Big Ten. The second one moved Smith one behind record-holder Braylon Edwards of Michigan. Bo Jackson ran for 107 yards and two second-half touchdowns to ice the game. Maryland used a 52-yard pick-six by Daniel Wingate to pull Maryland (2-4, 0-3) within 31-16 with 5:12 left in the third quarter. Maryland QB Malik Washington completed 12 of 25 passes for 64 yards. No. 7 Indiana 20, Nebraska 17 Josh Hoover hit Nick Marsh for two long touchdown passes and rallied the Hoosiers to a Big Ten victory over the Cornhuskers in Lincoln, Neb. Hoover completed 12 of 22 passes for 263 yards and two scores as the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0) shrugged off their first deficit of the season to extend their winning streak to 22 games heading into next week's home showdown against Ohio State. Nebraska limited the nation's No. 9 rushing offense to 65 yards -- far below the Hoosiers' 252.6-yard average. Anthony Colandrea, whose 39-yard touchdown keeper gave Nebraska a 17-6 lead with 12:01 to go, finished with 263 passing yards and 47 rushing yards as the Huskers (5-1, 2-1) came up short against a Top 25 foe for the 31st consecutive time. No. 9 Ole Miss 52, Vanderbilt 17 Trinidad Chambliss threw three touchdown passes and the Rebels scored four touchdowns in a nine-minute span of the second quarter in a rout of the host Commodores in Nashville, Tenn. Chambliss completed 20 of 30 passes for 213 yards with an interception. He also accounted for a rushing touchdown. Deuce Alexander caught a 39-yard touchdown pass and Shekai Mills-Knight produced a touchdown run of 35 yards for Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1). Jared Curtis returned from a one-week absence due to a knee injury to pass for 222 yards and a touchdown for Vanderbilt (3-3, 0-3), but he also committed three turnovers, two of which led to touchdowns during the second-quarter blitz. Kentucky 35, No. 10 LSU 34 (OT) Kenny Minchey drove the Wildcats to a tying field goal at the end of regulation and ran in the decisive two-point conversion in overtime as they defeated the Tigers in SEC play in Lexington, Ky. CJ Baxter rushed for 123 yards and two touchdowns, Minchey passed for 246 yards and the Wildcats (5-1, 3-1) won by the same score on a two-point overtime conversion as they did the previous Saturday at South Carolina. Sam Leavitt passed for 275 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, Jackson Harris caught one of those scoring passes and tossed one of his own for LSU (4-2, 1-2). No. 12 Utah 41, Kansas 24 Wayshawn Parker ran for 171 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Utes to a victory over the Jayhawks in Salt Lake City. It marked Parker's second straight game with more than 170 rushing yards after he posted a career-high 174 yards on the ground in Utah's win at Iowa State on Sept. 26. Devon Dampier completed 23 of 30 passes for 238 yards and three touchdowns to help the Utes (5-0, 2-0 Big 12) keep their record unblemished. Dampier added 68 yards and a score on the ground. Ricky Johnson led the Utah receivers with a season-high 104 yards and a touchdown on five catches. Isaiah Marshall was 19 of 37 for 333 passing yards and two touchdowns to lead Kansas. Cam Pickett, in his third game, tallied a season-high 134 yards on eight catches for the Jayhawks (2-3, 0-2), who outscored the Utes 17-7 in the second quarter to cut the halftime deficit to 21-17 and trailed 27-24 late in the third quarter. No. 21 UCLA 17, No. 13 Oregon 15 Wayne Knight rushed for a touchdown and caught another while the Bruins' defense stuffed a late two-point conversion attempt to earn a Big Ten win over the Ducks in Eugene, Ore. UCLA (5-0, 3-0 Big Ten) had not won in Autzen Stadium since 2004, but Knight's 9-yard score off a Ty Dieffenbach pass in the third quarter gave the Bruins a 17-6 lead that proved to be enough of a cushion to snap their eight-game losing streak on Oregon's field. Knight finished with 22 carries for 103 yards and caught three passes for 12 yards. Oregon (3-2, 1-1) battled back in the fourth quarter after Brock Thomas replaced quarterback Dylan Raiola, who started in place of injured Dante Moore. Thomas hit 11 of 15 passes for 156 yards, which included a 44-yard touchdown strike to Evan Stewart that pulled the Ducks within two with 2:16 to go. After a facemask penalty gave Oregon another chance from the 1-yard line, UCLA's Tyson Ford stuffed Jordon Davison's rush on the subsequent attempt. No. 14 Missouri 27, Texas A&M 6 Jamal Roberts rushed for 222 yards and two touchdowns, and the Tigers kept the Aggies out of the end zone in the SEC victory at Columbia, Mo. Roberts had 211 rushing yards a week ago against then-No. 8 Florida. On Saturday, Missouri (5-1, 2-1) intercepted Marcel Reed twice, getting one pick apiece from Trajen Greco and Elijah Dotson. The Tigers allowed 216 total yards, including only 29 on the ground. Texas A&M (3-3, 1-3), which has lost three of its past four games, trailed 10-3 at halftime and played effectively on defense until the second half, when Roberts and the Mizzou running game appeared to grind down the Aggies. Reed finished 19-of-39 passing for 187 yards. No. 15 Tennessee 24, Arkansas 17 DeSean Bishop's 8-yard touchdown run with 1:57 remaining led the Volunteers past the Razorbacks in Fayetteville, Ark., for Tennessee's first road win against Arkansas since 2001. Bishop had 19 carries for 138 yards and George MacIntyre was 18-for-29 passing for 247 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in his first start for the Volunteers (5-1, 2-1 SEC) as he replaced injured true freshman Faizon Brandon. KJ Jackson completed 15 of 27 passes for 155 yards with one touchdown for Arkansas (5-1, 2-1). Cam Settles led a balanced Razorback running game with 50 of the team's 133 rushing yards. South Carolina 38, No. 16 Florida 19 Quarterback LaNorris Sellers fired four touchdown passes and rushed for a score as the Gamecocks broke a three-game losing streak with an upset of the Gators in Gainesville, Fla. After blowing a 17-point lead in a home overtime loss last week against Kentucky, the Gamecocks (3-3, 1-3 SEC) snapped an eight-game conference losing streak as Sellers went 23 of 35 for 279 yards, with no interceptions. Nyck Harbor had 83 receiving yards and a touchdown on four catches. The Gators (4-2, 2-2) lost their second straight game as Aaron Philo was 21 of 28 for 227 yards and a touchdown, with one interception. Bailey Stockton had 127 yards and a score on eight receptions. Florida's Jadan Baugh (15 carries, 59 yards) scored his NCAA-best 12th rushing touchdown of the season in the fourth quarter. No. 18 Oklahoma State 42, UCF 28, Drew Mestemaker threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for a third as the Cowboys pulled away in the fourth quarter for the Big 12 triumph in Stillwater, Okla. With Oklahoma State (4-1, 2-0) clinging to a 27-21 edge early in the fourth quarter, Evan Jackson returned a deflected backward pass 28 yards for a touchdown to give the Cowboys a 35-21 lead with 10:32 to go. After Oklahoma State stuffed a fourth-and-1 play, Mestemaker hit Wyatt Young for a 5-yard score to break it open. Keyone Jenkins completed 30 of 42 passes for 265 yards and four touchdowns for UCF (3-3, 1-2). Josh Derry caught 11 passes for 84 yards and one score while Caden Piening added seven receptions for 60 yards and a score. No. 19 USC 31, Penn State 23 Jayden Maiava passed for 301 yards and three touchdowns as the Trojans handed the Nittany Lions a third straight conference loss with a win in University Park, Pa. Maiava threw a TD pass to Trent Mosley (nine catches, 111 yards), who had missed the previous three games, and also connected on scoring passes to Tanook Hines and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt. King Miller took care of matters on the ground for the Trojans (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten), rushing for 102 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Rocco Becht threw for 289 yards and a score for Penn State (3-3, 0-3). The Nittany Lions' rushing attack totaled just 68 yards on 31 attempts in front of a whiteout crowd of 114,419. No. 22 Houston 35, Kansas State 16 Conner Weigman threw for 242 yards and four touchdowns, all to Patrick Overmyer, as the Cougars cruised to a victory over the Wildcats in a Big 12 game in Manhattan, Kan. Overmyer caught eight passes for 83 yards, including touchdowns of 1, 2, 8 and 2 yards. Makhi Hughes rushed for 78 yards and a score, and Re'Shaun Sanford II added 90 yards on the ground for Houston (5-1, 2-1 Big 12), which led 28-3 early in the third quarter. For the Wildcats (3-2, 0-2), Avery Johnson completed 16 of 30 passes for 182 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Garrett Oakley and Jaron Tibbs each caught a touchdown pass. North Carolina 21, No. 25 Pitt 17 Billy Edwards Jr. threw for two touchdowns as the Tar Heels recorded the upset of the Panthers in an Atlantic Coast Conference game in Pittsburgh, giving second-year coach Bill Belichick his first victory against a ranked team. Edwards completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards and two interceptions. The Tar Heels' (3-2, 1-1 Atlantic Coast Conference) go-ahead touchdown came on Edwards' 75-yard touchdown pass play to Shamar Easter with 12:36 remaining in the game. La'Vell Wright ran for two touchdowns for Pitt (5-1, 2-1). Holden Geriner was 27-for-44 passing for 219 yards, with two interceptions, in his first start following a season-ending knee injury suffered by Mason Heintschel a week earlier. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nico Hischier scores milestone goal, leads Devils past Canucks
item.description: Nico Hischier scored twice on the power play, including his 200th career goal, and the New Jersey Devils rallied to beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-1 on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nico Hischier scored twice on the power play, including his 200th career goal, and the New Jersey Devils rallied to beat the Vancouver Canucks 4-1 on Saturday afternoon in Newark, N.J. Jake Allen made 20 saves in his 500th career game to get the win as New Jersey snapped a two-game losing skid. Jesper Bratt had a goal and an assist, Jesper Boqvist also scored and Jack Hughes had two assists for the Devils, who finished with three goals on the power play to claim their second win of the season. Hischier, who signed a five-year, $58.5 million deal in the offseason, also had an assist. Linus Karlsson had a goal while Leevi Merilainen and Kevin Lankinen combined to stop 33 shots for the Canucks, who suffered their third consecutive loss. Paul Cotter, the NHL's Third Star of the Week, was held pointless in his first game with the Canucks against his former team. The teams traded power-play goals to open the scoring in the first period. Karlsson gave the Canucks a 1-0 lead with a power play goal on a one-timer after taking a pass from Brock Boeser. Hischier busted out of an early slump to score his first point of the season and 200th goal to tie it 1-1 with Vancouver forward Jonathan Lekkerimaki off for high-sticking. The Devils then recorded their first regulation lead of the season by capitalizing on a Canucks miscue in the Vancouver zone. Amadeus Lombardi stole the puck from Canucks defenseman Filip Hronek, then took a shot that generated a rebound which was poked in by forward Boqvist to make it 2-1 at 16:24 of the first period. Boqvist's goal came against Lankinen, who entered the game after starter Merilainen sustained an equipment malfunction when his skate blade fell out. Merilainen left the game with 5:27 remaining in the first and returned for the start of the second period. Bratt took advantage of a mad scramble in the Canucks' crease early in the second, scoring on the power play from a sharp angle with a shot that ricocheted off a couple Vancouver players into the net to give the Devils a two-goal lead. Hischier finished off a tic-tac-toe passing play for his second power play goal with just 10 seconds left in the second to make it 4-1. --Field Level Media

item.title: Une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport de Ryad fait douze morts, selon des sources
item.description: Une attaque contre l'aéroport de Ryad a fait douze morts et des dizaines de blessés samedi, selon trois sources au fait du dossier, tandis que tous les vols ont été déroutés.
